calibrated_on: ubuntu-latest (GitHub Actions), Ruby 4.0.7, rbs 4.2.0, release-gate-frozen-corpus @ run 36312373173
note: Linux CI measurements of this checkout's engine over the frozen corpus v0.4.0: the tree at that tag, unpacked with git archive (#1507). allocations is the tight signal; wall_s is a coarse backstop. bench/README.md lists what the corpus run does not reproduce: gems' own sig/, the core RBS and Ruby, which come from the run, and a user-global BUNDLE_PATH. Switched on 2026-09-27 from Rigor's own growing lib (ADR-50 WD4 records the growth). The previous baseline (the v0.4.0 cut, run 36278383180) measured the v0.4.0 engine over the v0.4.0 checkout with its bundle: 42,721,526 allocations, wall_s 44.179, peak_rss_kb 563,060. Its +80.5% over v0.3.9 was accepted as a whole, and the engine's own +19.1% was separated only afterwards (#1469). This run measures master d709a0419 (v0.4.0 plus #1491, #1496, #1508, #1509 and #1511) over the v0.4.0 tree: 38,543,742 allocations, wall_s 46.083, peak_rss_kb 584,384. The same engine read 38,586,535 allocations on macOS (+0.11%), and the two CI reps differed by 228 objects. No per-PR "Engine allocations" warning precedes it: that job landed in #1512, after the engine changes measured here. The band is a budget for the engine cost added since this calibration. Refresh on the same corpus after an engine improvement by measuring the improving PR's own merge commit, and list in the new note every per-PR warning since this calibration with its answer; an unanswered one needs the user's ruling first. A red cut clears only by attributing the rise and recalibrating on the same corpus on the user's ruling. After each release the corpus advances to the new tag. bench/README.md and the rigor-release-prep skill carry the procedures. Sampling rule (#987): each gate run takes 2 reps per target, EACH IN A FRESH PROCESS (VmHWM is a per-process high-water mark, so an in-process rep can never report lower RSS, and a warm rep's wall is not comparable with this cold baseline), and records the LOWER of the reps for wall_s and peak_rss_kb while allocations and diagnostics are taken from the first rep unreduced. Measure a recalibration the same way -- bench/baseline.updated.json is already reduced, so committing it preserves the rule.
